author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, shown by first name then last name. All specialties appear at once, and the page is reached by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty page is opened, then every one of them is listed by its stored name, all on the one page
given a specialty that veterinarians hold, when the specialty page is opened, then every holder is listed under it by first name then last name
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the specialty page is opened, then it is listed with no veterinarian under it
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty page is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on it
given any other page of the system, when it is rendered, then it carries no link to the specialty page
non_goals: a navigation entry for the specialty page, or a link to it from any other page
managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2 unchanged)
searching or filtering specialties (NG-9 unchanged); the whole list is present
showing the specialty list a page at a time
listing veterinarians who hold no specialty
notes: Owner decisions quoted from intake-decision (handoff.jsonl line 1): 'A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2 is unchanged).' and 'The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come as a follow-up request.' The owner named the address: 'GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it.' No Non-Goals row changes, so no scope_overrides. Two boundary readings taken narrowly and recorded in the PRD: (1) the page itself still carries the navigation every page carries per REQ-SYS-001 - only the navigation gains no entry for it; (2) presentation order is unspecified, recorded as an open question rather than assumed. Fixed page wording falls under REQ-LANG-002 (eleven message bundles), which this request does not override. Specialty names render as stored.

Contracts rows added for SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyHolders, and SpecialtyController; Vet, Specialty, and VetRepository now also carry REQ-VET-003. Placement decisions: (1) the route lives in a new package-private SpecialtyController rather than VetController, keeping one controller per HTTP surface and each controller's dependency set minimal (architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog, Web controller row; Naming row for controllers); (2) the specialty-to-holders derivation lives in the SpecialtyHolders value object, not in the controller, since the Design Validation Checklist bars a new business rule in a web controller and the recorded controller deviation does not extend to new rules. risks.mitigation: the derivation lives in SpecialtyHolders and is unit-tested without MockMvc (architecture-principles.md Design Validation Checklist, no-business-rule-in-controller item)

risks.mitigation: it is a record whose holder list is copied and wrapped unmodifiable at construction; the framework-mapped persistence-entity exception does not cover it (architecture-principles.md Scoped exception)

risks.mitigation: every literal goes through a #{} key present in all eleven bundles (docs/prd.md REQ-LANG-002; I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails otherwise)

notes: Verdict rationale: every element instantiates a catalog pattern already in force (Repository, Value object, Web controller) with a sibling in the tree; the only delta worth recording is the first read path for Specialty and the placement of the grouping. No ADR: each choice is reversible and follows an existing brief, so none meets the hard-to-reverse-plus-real-trade-off bar. Ordering: docs/prd.md records presentation order as an open product question, so any order satisfies the criteria; design fixes a deterministic one (specialties by stored name, holders by last name then first name) for stable rendering and stable tests, consistent with Vet.getSpecialties() and PetTypeRepository. This is a design choice, not a product answer — the PRD open question stands. Open question recorded rather than raised, per the standing note that no further product answer will arrive: whether an unheld specialty renders an explicit localized 'none' (as the vet list does for a vet with no specialty) or simply nothing under it. Both readings satisfy the acceptance criterion; the narrow reading is 'listed with no veterinarian under it', so either is in scope and the implementer picks one. Do not edit fragments/layout.html — a navigation entry there would breach the last acceptance criterion. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. docs/system-design.md edits this dispatch: three new Contracts rows, REQ-VET-003 added to the Vet, Specialty, and VetRepository rows, a 'The specialty page' paragraph under the Contracts invariants note, and one provenance sentence marking post-survey rows as pipeline decisions.
